name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
previewNote: Preview: the main rates for this country come from official or professional tax guides, but contributions and some thresholds are still being verified. Use the result as a rough guide and confirm with the tax authority.

registry.name: Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property

legalStatuses.label: Registered business name
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.
legalStatuses.registeredAt: Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property
legalStatuses.feeNote: Confirm the current registration fee with the registry.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.registeredAt: Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property
legalStatuses.feeNote: Incorporation costs more than a business name. Confirm the current fees with the registry.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Inland Revenue and get your tax number (TIN)
launchSteps.plain: A number that identifies you to the tax office. You need it for almost every other step.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
launchSteps.plain: If you trade under any name other than your own, you must register it. Search the name at the Registrar first.

launchSteps.label: Register the business name, or incorporate the company, with the Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property
launchSteps.plain: A sole trader registers the business name. A company must be incorporated first.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Social Security Board
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people must register and contribute. It gives access to a pension and other benefits.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register as an employer and prepare monthly payments
launchSteps.plain: With employees you pay social security (and income tax withheld, where it applies) each month. Ask the authorities for your deadlines.

launchSteps.label: Register for VAT
launchSteps.plain: Required once your yearly sales reach the VAT threshold (EC$400,000). Register with the Inland Revenue.

contributions.label: Social Security
contributions.plain: Social security gives access to a pension and other benefits. Self-employed people register with the Social Security Board. The rate and ceiling are still being verified.

vat.label: Value Added Tax
vat.registerNote: Registration is required once your annual taxable supplies pass the threshold. The exact amount is still being verified.
vat.filingNote: VAT returns are filed monthly, by the 15th of the following month.

calendar.quarterlyTextCorporate: Pay your advance corporation tax instalment.
calendar.monthlyText: Ask the Inland Revenue when your advance tax payments fall due.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: File the annual returns that apply to you. Ask the Inland Revenue Department for the deadlines.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay social security (and income tax withheld, where it applies) for the previous month.
calendar.vatText: If registered for VAT: file your return every month, by the 15th of the following month.

notes: Saint Kitts and Nevis has no personal income tax. An unincorporated business tax and a Housing and Social Development Levy may apply: they are not included in your estimate.
